details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects a 1.3% contraction in economic output for the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan in 2026. This downturn is attributed to an ongoing war involving the US, Israel, and Iran, which has disrupted energy production, shipping, tourism, and trade, and negatively impacted investor confidence. A rebound to 6.6% growth is anticipated in 2027, assuming a de-escalation of the conflict.
title: IMF: Middle East Economic Output to Shrink by 1.3% in 2026

details: Global financial markets are experiencing a "risk-off" sentiment following underwhelming corporate earnings from major tech companies like Meta and Tesla, contributing to declines in Asian and US tech stocks. Simultaneously, escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are driving up oil prices. Amidst this cautious environment, Bitcoin has fallen by 2.66% to approximately $82,400 USD.
title: Bitcoin Dips as Global Markets Enter Risk-Off Mode After Earnings, Mideast Tensions

details: Major cryptocurrency exchanges, including Blockchain.com, Binance US, Coinbase, Crypto.com, and Gemini, are expanding into prediction markets. This strategic move aims to diversify revenue streams in response to a prolonged downturn in digital asset prices, with Bitcoin and Ether seeing significant declines over the past year, and reduced trading volumes. Prediction markets allow speculation on various outcomes, including economic events and interest rate decisions.
title: Crypto Exchanges Pivot to Prediction Markets as Digital Asset Trading Cools

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has launched "Project Pontes," a distributed ledger system for interbank tokenized securities trading, and the European Union is expected to finalize a legislative proposal for a retail digital euro (CBDC) by the end of the year. These initiatives position Europe at the forefront of developing a public monetary architecture for the digital age, driven by concerns over financial sovereignty.
title: Europe Forges Ahead with Digital Euro and Tokenized Finance Infrastructure

details: Ethereum (ETH) is trading around $2,400, marking a 2.3% drop in the last 24 hours and a 12.6% decline over the past 30 days. Despite bouncing twice from the critical $2,300 support level in October, sustained selling pressure is evident. Cumulative net inflows for spot Ether ETFs have decreased from $14 billion to $12.8 billion between September 28 and October 21, indicating a continuous outflow of capital. A daily close below $2,313 with significant ETF outflows could lead to further price depreciation.
title: Ethereum Price Analysis: ETH Battles $2,300 Support Amid ETF Outflows
